nodes.summary: A sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ with values in a type $\alpha$ is eventually periodic if there are natural numbers $p > 0$ (a period) and $n_0$ (a preperiod) such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Eventually periodic sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type. A sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is called ultimately periodic exactly when it is eventually periodic; the two terms name the same notion.
nodes.title: Ultimately periodic sequences

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set, $F : S \to S$ a map and $r : \mathbb{N} \to S$ a sequence with $r(n + 1) = F(r(n))$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $r$ is eventually periodic.
nodes.title: Orbits in a finite set are eventually periodic

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence and let $p > 0$ be a natural number with $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $u$ is eventually periodic.
nodes.title: Periodic sequences are eventually periodic

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type and $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ a sequence. If there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0$ such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$, then $u$ is eventually periodic.
nodes.title: Explicit period and preperiod give eventual periodicity

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type. If a sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is eventually periodic, then there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0$ such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Period and preperiod of an eventually periodic sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
